title: 눈 means EYE and SNOW 😂 (snow in my eye = 눈에 눈) #learnkorean
caption:
눈 (nun) = eye 👁 AND snow ❄️
Same word, two things — so when snow lands in your eye, that's 눈에 눈 (nu-ne nun) 😂

Words in this video:
이거, 눈! (i-geo, nun!) = This is 눈 (eye)!
저것도 눈! (jeo-geot-do nun!) = That's 눈 too (snow)!
눈에 눈! (nu-ne nun!) = Snow in my eye!
안 보여~! (an bo-yeo~!) = I can't see~!

Tip: In careful standard Korean, 눈 for "snow" has a long vowel [nuːn], but in everyday speech most people say both the same way.
안 보여 is casual — with someone older, say 안 보여요 (an bo-yeo-yo).

alt: A needle-felt miniature Seoul alley at dusk as the first snow begins. Mongle, a coral felt blob mascot with no arms, looks up at the sky and says 눈! while a felt Korean young man in a grey padded coat points at his own eye and asks 눈? He explains 이거, 눈! (this is 눈 — eye), Mongle answers 저것도 눈! (that's 눈 too — snow). A big felt snowflake falls and sticks right on Mongle's eye: 눈에 눈! (snow in my eye!). The friend laughs. Labels show 눈 = eye and 눈 = snow. A second snowflake lands on Mongle's other eye — 안 보여~! (I can't see~!) — and Mongle wobbles blindly.
